title: Destroy stages can wait on external operations
detail: A tick in which a hook reports pending is recorded as a progressed event with pending true and does not count as a failed attempt. The wait is bounded: once 60 minutes (DESTRUCTION_STAGE_MAX_PENDING_MS) have passed since the attempt's stage-started event, a pending tick fails the attempt with "still pending", and the stage is abandoned after its usual maxAttempts, so a stage waits at most maxAttempts x 60 minutes. Ticks without progress and without pending still count as failed attempts. stage-started events now carry startedAt from the sweep clock.

title: Destruction sweep no longer wakes a sleeping app
detail: The run-tenant-destruction cron declares wakesSleepingApp false, so its per-minute schedule does not keep a sleeping shared app awake. A due destruction runs on the next wake, for example the daily maintenance window. Its scheduler id changes to scheduler-nowake-tenant-lifecycle-job-run-tenant-destruction; the old scheduler is removed on the first start.

title: archiveAndDeleteTenantRows for tenant-destroy hooks
detail: @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/tenant-lifecycle exports archiveAndDeleteTenantRows(ctx, table, aggregateType, escapeHatchReason), which archives each row's event stream and then deletes the tenant's rows, plus the TENANT_DESTROY_ARCHIVED_BY and TENANT_DESTROY_ARCHIVE_REASON constants. inbound-mail-foundation uses the helper, billing-foundation the constants.

title: Tenant destroy keeps user keys of members in other live tenants
detail: The subject-keys stage erases user keys only for members without a membership in another tenant whose status is not destroyed. The tenant and tenant-record keys are erased as before.

title: Destroy sweep keeps a minimum time slice per tenant
detail: With many tenants in destroying state the shared tick budget no longer shrinks a tenant's slice below two seconds, so chunking hooks make progress instead of failing the stage as no-progress attempts.

title: One sweep tick shares a single stage budget between all destroying tenants
detail: The destruction sweep used to give every destroying tenant its own full stage budget, so a few large tenants stretched one tick far beyond the minute cron window and the following ticks were skipped. The tick budget is now divided evenly over the destroying tenants. Each tenant's slice starts when that tenant's turn begins, so an overrun by one tenant never leaves the next ones with a zero slice. runNextDestructionStage accepts an optional deadlineAt.

title: tenant-lifecycle/testing exports runTenantDestructionSweep, seedDestroyingTenant and driveDestructionToCompletion
Tenant destroy stages resume partial progress next tick; hooks may return { done: false } and get deadlineAt; file hooks work in chunks
detail:
Tenant destroy stages resume partial progress in the next sweep tick instead of burning failed attempts
A tenant with tens of thousands of files used to exhaust the stage's three attempts and leave the DSGVO destroy stuck. Destroy hooks (`destroyTenant`, EXT_TENANT_DATA `destroy`) may now return `{ done: false, processed }` and receive `deadlineAt` in their ctx; the runner records a `tenant-destruction-stage-progressed` event in the tenant stream and continues the stage next tick without counting a failed attempt. Hooks returning nothing stay valid. The `fileRef` row purge and the storage prefix wipe work in chunks against that deadline.

title: Boot warns when files is mounted without files-tenant-data
detail: files-tenant-data is opt-in, so an app with tenant-lifecycle and files that forgot it silently left fileRef rows and stored binaries behind on tenant destroy. tenant-lifecycle now logs a boot warning in that case. Action: mount createFilesTenantDataFeature(), or ignore the warning if the app erases files itself.

title: Tenant destroy: a stage tick without progress counts as a failed attempt; done:false requires processed
tenant destroy deletes handed-over binaries via the uploader's provider, trigger reports invalid payloads distinctly, mail failure logs redact addresses
detail: A tenant destroy deletes a handed-over binary through the file provider of the tenant that uploaded it, not the destroyed tenant's. `jobs:write:trigger` answers a broken or non-object JSON payload with `job_invalid_payload` instead of `job_not_manual`. Grouped metrics restrict their stack and series queries to the top groups. The notes and folders sections filter by `entityType` on the server. A failed mail dispatch logs the adapter error without email addresses.
